q: What is the thinking distance at 50 km/h?
Calculate the total stopping distance at 90 km/h.
Describe how each distance changes with speed.
Thinking distance rises steadily (in proportion); braking distance rises much faster (roughly with the square of the speed).
A driver using a phone has a reaction time twice as long. Calculate the stopping distance at 50 km/h, and explain the danger.
Thinking 28 m + braking 16 m = 44 m instead of 30 m: the car travels 14 m further before stopping, enough to hit a pedestrian.
